input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: __aexit__ delegates to __exit__ with None for the exception type, value and traceback instead of forwarding the arguments it received
- failure path: an exception raised inside `async with attempt:` reaches __aexit__, which calls __exit__ with (None, None, None); __exit__ takes its success branch, records no failed outcome and returns None, so the exception propagates out of the async with and past the retry loop: the attempt is never recorded as failed and no retry happens

Reviewer finding
- description: __aexit__ discards the actual exception arguments and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so the AttemptManager never sees the exception raised inside the async with block.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception is raised inside `async with attempt:` (e.g., a failed I/O call). The sync __exit__ is designed to receive exc_type/exc_value to call set_exception on the retry state; passing None makes it record a successful result instead. Mechanism: the failure is silently swallowed and set_result(None) is recorded, so the retry loop believes the attempt succeeded and never retries. Impact: retries are silently skipped and failed operations are reported as successful, a silent wrong result.
critique: Both describe the same faulty operation: __aexit__ calls __exit__(None, None, None) instead of forwarding the exception arguments, so __exit__ takes its success branch and no retry happens. The finding wrongly says the exception is silently swallowed, when the label says it propagates out because __exit__ returns None. That is an error in the downstream impact only; the defect and mechanism are the same.
